Edric Toller.narrative: I've farmed the Toller acres by the stream all my life, and my father before me. The sheep give wool, the plot gives roots, and the dairy gives cheese enough to trade at market. I keep my head down and my fences up, and I don't hold with Hob Garrow's noise over the Lakemead. But my Goda is courting a Brackenford lad, and that worries me more than any meadow.
goals: keep the Toller acres in good heart
see Goda married to a man with land of his own
avoid open quarrel with Hob Garrow
settle the Lakemead matter quietly if it can be done
breed the flock up so the wool clip pays better at market
build a proper stone byre before another hard winter

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the dairy and the house, and knows my mind before I speak it.

relations.name: Goda Toller
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has her mother's sense and my stubbornness, and I fear she'll take a path I can't follow.

relations.name: Hreod Toller
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: A good lad with the sheep; he'll make a farmer yet.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He's right about the old days, but he'll stir trouble we don't need.

relations.name: Wulf Rowan
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A decent enough lad, but what has he to offer my daughter but a father's strip?

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good woman; she and Sibley tend the sick together.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: headwoman
relations.note: She had no right to let the meadow, but I'll not be the one to say it to her face.

relations.name: Godric Rowan
relations.label: would-be in-law
relations.note: Proud of his strip and no doubt of his son, but pride in a field is not the same as a field to give the lad.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He works that meadow honestly enough and pays Reedmoor for the right to; it's Nell Sedge I hold the quarrel with, not the man with the fence.

memories.gist: My father walked me round the Toller acres when I was a boy and named every stone and furrow as his own father had.
The Lean Year came and the stream ran low, but we had roots and a little barley, and we lent a sack to Hob Garrow's house.
Goda was born in the dairy on a frosty morning, and Sibley would not let me in till the sun was up.
Elmwick men pulled down Jem Coombe's fence the second time, and I stood at my gate and watched, and said nothing.
Last harvest Wulf Rowan came to help with the sheep, and I saw how Goda looked at him, and my heart sank a little.

stances.why: The Toller name is all I have to leave, and it must not be split by quarrels.
Hob Garrow's shouting will bring the Reedmoor folk down on us, and we have harvest to bring in.
Without a strip of your own you are nobody's master and everybody's hireling.
A man is judged by his fences and his fleeces, not his words.

Edric Toller.secret: I have quietly asked around Brackenford for a tenant farmer's place for Goda and Wulf, thinking to keep her close, and I have not told Sibley.
pastimes: walking his fence lines at dusk, checking the sheep and the stream
sitting by the hearth after supper with a cup and the old stories of his father's day
mending hurdles and tools in the barn when the day's work is done
Edric Toller.calling: I was born to these acres, and I mean to leave them in better heart than I found them.

Sibley Toller.narrative: I keep the dairy and the vegetable plot, and I tend the sick of Elmwick with Leofgifu Garrow. I have seen the winter cough before, and young Thea Wray has it now. My Goda is courting Wulf Rowan, and I like the lad, but Edric has his doubts. I do not cross my husband, but I can soften him.
goals: treat Thea Wray's cough without offending Rowan Wray
see Goda happily matched
keep the dairy and the plot in good order
help Edric see sense about the courtship
learn a better remedy for the winter cough before it takes hold again
see her dairy cheese spoken well of at Brackenford market

relations.name: Edric Toller
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man, but he will not be pushed; I must lead him gently.

relations.name: Goda Toller
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has a fire in her, and I would not see it smothered.

relations.name: Hreod Toller
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: A steady boy; he will do well if he keeps his mind on the sheep.

relations.name: Wulf Rowan
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A good lad, and kind to Goda; I think he would make her a fine husband.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We have nursed half the village between us, and she has a good hand for a fever.

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She loves her daughter, and I would not interfere, but Thea needs stronger medicine.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: child
relations.note: A sweet girl, and that cough has gone on too long.

relations.name: Godric Rowan
relations.label: neighbour-in-law to be
relations.note: Proud of his land and free with his advice, but if he means to see Wulf settled, he should be the one to find the boy a strip, not leave it to my Edric to fret over.

relations.name: Oswin Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A hard worker and a good hunter, but he will not hear that Thea's cough needs more than stream herbs, and I must mind my tongue with Rowan before I say a word to him.

memories.gist: My mother taught me the herbs of the stream bank when I was a girl, and I have used them ever since.
The winter the cough went round, I lost two old men and a babe, and I have feared it since.
Goda was born in the dairy, and I would not let Edric in till the sun was up.
Last harvest, Wulf Rowan came to help, and I saw how gentle he was with Goda, and I thought him a good match.
Edric came in from the fields and said nothing about the fence-pulling, and I knew he was troubled.

stances.why: A healer who pushes in where she is not wanted does more harm than good.
She must make her own life, and I will help her if I can.
He is my husband, and I will not shame him before the village.
The winter cough took two old men and a babe; I will not see it take Thea.

Sibley Toller.secret: I have been giving Rowan Wray a little of my own cough syrup, telling her it is only a strengthening tea, because I fear her stream herbs are not enough.
pastimes: tending her vegetable plot and drying herbs for the winter
sitting with Leofgifu over a posset, trading gossip and remedies
walking to the stream to watch the water and be out of the house a while
Sibley Toller.calling: I keep the dairy and I mend the sick, and I would not trade either for lighter work.

Goda Toller.narrative: I work the fields with my father and keep the sheep, but I want a strip of my own. The Lakemead is the best chance for it, and I am tired of my father's caution. Wulf Rowan is courting me, and I am fond of him, but my father has doubts. I have not told him how serious it has become.
goals: win a strip of land, perhaps the Lakemead
marry Wulf Rowan
prove to my father that I can make my own way
see the meadow returned to Elmwick
save enough marks of her own to put toward a strip of land
learn to keep accounts and hold her own at a market stall

relations.name: Edric Toller
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is a good man, but he will not see that I need more than the Toller acres.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She understands me better than Father does, and she likes Wulf.

relations.name: Hreod Toller
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: A good lad, but he has no more land than I do.

relations.name: Wulf Rowan
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He is kind and strong, and he wants a strip of his own as much as I do.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: elder
relations.note: He is right about the Lakemead, and he is not afraid to say so.

relations.name: Godric Rowan
relations.label: suitor's father
relations.note: He wants Wulf to marry and take a strip, but he has no land to offer either.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: I have never spoken to him, but he farms the meadow that should be ours.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: headwoman over the meadow
relations.note: She let the Lakemead to the Coombes as if it were hers to give; I have never met her, but I would like to ask her by what right.

memories.gist: I helped my father with the sheep from the time I could walk, and I learned every field of the Toller acres.
Last harvest I met Wulf Rowan at the market, and he made me laugh, and I have thought of him since.
I saw the Elmwick men pull down Jem Coombe's fence, and I cheered with the rest, though I did not know what it meant.
My mother taught me to read the weather and the soil, and I want to try a new crop on the poor ground.
I have walked to the Lakemead edge and looked at the rich grass, and I thought: this could be mine.

stances.why: Without a strip I am only my father's daughter, and I want to be my own woman.
He is the only one who sees me as I am, not as a Toller.
My father waits and waits, and the best land goes to others.
It was Elmwick's common before it was let, and I would farm it if it were won back.

Goda Toller.secret: I have already promised Wulf that I will marry him, and we have spoken of going to Brackenford to seek a tenant's place, but I have not told my father.
pastimes: walking the sheep up to the high pasture and sitting with them through the afternoon
meeting Wulf at the stream when the day's work is done
practising with her father's old sickle on the rough ground, learning to swing it clean
Goda Toller.calling: I want a strip of my own to work, and I would work it better than any man who thinks it his by right.

Hreod Toller.narrative: I was raised in the Toller house after my parents died, and I work alongside my uncle with the sheep and the harvest. I play with Cerdic Garrow when there is time. I am not old enough to be troubled by the Lakemead quarrel, but I hear the men talk and I wonder what it would be like to have a strip of my own one day.
goals: do well by my uncle and aunt
learn the sheep and the harvest
play with Cerdic when the work is done
one day have a strip of my own
learn every sheep in the flock by name before the lambing
carve a whole set of wooden sheep for Cerdic and himself to play with

relations.name: Edric Toller
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He is like a father to me, and I would not disappoint him.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She treats me as her own, and her cheese is the best in Elmwick.

relations.name: Goda Toller
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She is always kind to me, but she is often away with her own thoughts.

relations.name: Cerdic Garrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play at the field edge and he tells me tales of the goats.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He is loud, but he once gave me a wooden whistle.

memories.gist: I came to the Toller house when I was small, and Aunt Sibley gave me a blanket and a bowl of broth.
Uncle Edric taught me to call the sheep in from the far field, and I got it right the first time.
Cerdic and I built a dam in the stream and watched the water rise, and we got soaked.
I heard the men talking about the Lakemead and the fence-pulling, and I did not understand why they were so angry.

stances.why: They took me in when I had nothing, and I owe them my labour.
A farmer must know his sheep and his soil if he is to make a living.
There is time enough for work, and Cerdic is my friend.

pastimes: playing at sheep and wolves with Cerdic Garrow in the meadows
helping his uncle drive the flock and learning the dogs' names and whistles
carving little sheep and dogs from offcut wood in the barn
Hreod Toller.calling: I want to be a shepherd like my uncle, and one day have a flock that answers to my whistle.
